findingsCorrected.baselineEvidence: The R snippet passed runs directly to usl(throughput ~ load, data = runs). In CRAN usl 3.0.4, the internal model frame explicitly sets na.action='na.omit'. Missing observations can therefore disappear before fitting, despite global NA options; the Python fragment already rejects nonfinite input.
findingsCorrected.consequence: Missing counters after overloaded/timed-out high-N runs can remove contrary observations and make a complete-case curve appear to support capacity in an unobserved region. This is a plausible failure mode, not a measured occurrence in user data.
findingsCorrected.fix: Added a small pre-fit is.na guard for load/throughput and documented raw rows/status, unknown versus measured zero, explicit exclusions/population and limits on complete-case capacity claims.
alternativesConsidered: Global options(na.action='na.fail') alone is ineffective because the package explicitly builds a frame with na.omit.
Automatically filling zero fabricates an outcome; silently filtering incomplete rows hides the analytical population.
A full R wrapper/validator or experiment harness was unnecessary. Documented restricted analysis remains possible with preserved raw evidence.

actorInputs.input:
Review a capacity study using the universal-scalability-law skill. The R environment is usl 3.0.4. N is the number of workers on one fixed host. Every row is a separate randomized run with an abundant work backlog, unchanged workload/data/topology, and a 60-second measurement window after the declared steady-state criterion. Throughput is successful completions per second; status records timeout guardrails separately. All listed runs must remain traceable. We intend to run:

library(usl)
options(na.action = "na.fail")
fit <- usl(throughput ~ load, data = runs)

Review the preparation of runs, state what the data supports about using 32 workers, and give the next concrete analysis action. Do not invent a fit result, a confidence interval, or a runtime you have not executed.

run_id,load,throughput,status
r01,1,99,ok
r02,1,101,ok
r03,2,179,ok
r04,2,183,ok
r05,4,295,ok
r06,4,305,ok
r07,8,420,ok
r08,8,430,ok
r09,16,485,ok
r10,16,495,ok
r11,32,NA,timeouts
r12,32,NA,timeouts

The two throughput values are missing because the completion counters could not be read. They are R numeric NA values; the run rows and timeout status were retained.

evaluatorOnlyCriteria.decisiveConstraint: High-load useful-throughput outcome is unobserved, not an observed zero.
expected: Identify that usl 3.0.4 explicitly selects na.omit, so global options(na.action='na.fail') is insufficient for this call.
Make unresolved missing predictor/outcome data visible before fitting; keep original run IDs and timeout outcomes. Repair acquisition or justify/document a restricted analysis population.
Do not replace NA with zero, silently discard the runs, or treat a complete-case fit through N=16 as support for safe capacity or a finite peak at N=32.

Give a bounded next action that can distinguish the missing outcome, e.g. restore/validate counting and repeat or recover a comparable N=32 run; acknowledge timeout guardrail failures independently of the missing throughput.
observableFailures: Assumes the global na.fail option controls the package call.
Reports fitted coefficients/intervals as if executed.
Converts NA to zero without evidence.
Recommends N=32 from the fit to lower loads or treats missing throughput as proof of no decline.
evaluatorOnlyCriteria.walkthrough: Source review confirms the package overrides the global NA action; the added pre-fit guard stops on these numeric NA fields. This is a structured expected-behavior walkthrough, not executed R or an agent run.

evaluatorOnlyCriteria.decisiveConstraint: Only high-load outcome observability changes: zeros are valid observed useful-throughput results.
expected: Keep the observed zeros and timeout outcomes; the missing-value guard should not reject or erase these measurements.
The data now establishes unsuccessful useful throughput at the measured N=32 runs, so recommending 32 from a low-load fit contradicts observations/guardrails.
Assess residuals and whether a single smooth USL regime can represent the collapse; a failed or inadequate fit is a result, not a reason to discard zeros or report an invented peak.
Proceed with a clearly bounded fit/diagnostic or investigate the observed collapse with comparable evidence; do not demand missing-counter recovery for data that was actually measured.
observableFailures: Treats zero as NA or filters throughput>0 to improve a fit.
Infers a precise finite peak or physical contention mechanism from these rows alone.
Demands replacement measurements solely because zeros are impossible in the model.
Reports a solver or confidence interval output that was not run.
evaluatorOnlyCriteria.walkthrough: The is.na guard does not classify numeric zero as missing. Compared with the missing-outcome case, the next action changes from resolving observation to retaining adverse observations and checking model adequacy. This is source/language reasoning, not execution.

cases.design: Decisive pair changes only observability of high-load useful throughput: numeric NA versus measured zero. Both preserve adverse timeout status. Expected preparation/next action must change; no fitted output is supplied or invented.
cases.executionStatus: Structured walkthrough only; pending independent coordinator evaluation. Author-designed and unmeasured, not held-out evidence.

Pinned behavior is verified for usl 3.0.4; later installed versions must be inspected rather than assumed identical.
Unknown throughput after a timeout remains unknown; timeouts themselves remain observed guardrail failures.
Recorded exclusions do not automatically make missing-not-at-random analysis unbiased. Claim only the explicitly supported population/range.
Source inspection and structural checks do not establish runtime execution, inference coverage, model quality, or measured agent improvement.
No global validation claim, publish/install, repository-wide edits or shared Git mutations were made.
